question: What was the text of the official statement of 19 May 1986 about the damaged reactor?
answer: An accident occurred at Vereskovo NPS; one reactor was damaged; measures are being taken; aid is given; a government commission was set up.

question: What were the sentences handed down on 29 July 1987?
answer: Hrytsenko 10, Savchenko 10, Zuev 10, G. A. Morozov 5, Sidorenko 3, Fedorov 2 years.

question: What dose was the max for military and civilian participants in 1986?
answer: 25 rem (0.25 Sv) as a single exposure for the period of work.

question: Where was the high-range VR-1000 No. 0012 kept before the accident and when did it reach Unit 4?
answer: In the safe of the Unit 1 dosimetry room; the key was at the dosimetry engineer's home; safe opened 03:40; instrument at Unit 4 at 03:50 on 17 May.

question: What did Academician Nikitin observe during the helicopter flight on 18 May?
answer: Building destroyed above +35, upper plate tilted, core open, glow (burning graphite), graphite and fuel on roofs, 500 R/h at 200 m.

question: What is the estimated design life of the Shelter per the July 1987 assessment?
answer: 20-30 years.

question: Who led the clearing of the Unit 3 roof and how many servicemen took part?
answer: Capt. O. Panchenko; about 3,400 servicemen, 20 Sep - 1 Oct 1986.

question: When was the separation wall between Unit 3 and Unit 4 completed?
Give the full maintenance history of U4-MCP-03 from 1984 to the accident.
answer: Feb 1984 seal inspection; vibration rose from ~Jul 1985, above 7.1 mm/s (Sep balancing; Oct load limited); bearing housing batch 82-07 defect acknowledged by Severny (Jul 1985); bearing replaced 18-25 Nov 1985 (WP-85-1146) with improved type, 2.7 mm/s after; stable Jan-May 1986 (measured in um); running on the night; cavitation hypothesis examined and rejected; destroyed.

question: Reconstruct the sequence from the start of the power reduction to the explosions.
answer: 15 May 23:00 start; 16 May 13:05 TG-7 off at 1,600 MW; 14:00 ECCS isolated, dispatcher hold; 23:10 resumed; 00:00 shift change; 00:28 drop to ~30 MW; 01:03 ~200 MW; 01:05 MCP-4 & -8 started; 01:22:30 ORM ~7; 01:23 trips blocked; 01:31:05 TG-8 valves closed; 01:31:41 AZ-5; 01:31:44 surge; ~01:31:45 and ~01:31:48 explosions.

question: What happened to the Unit 4 night shift (Shift 5) staff?
answer: Tkachuk d. 2 Jun 1986; Lavrinenko d. 31 May; Kalinin d. 14 Jun; Melnyk ARS III, survived, retired on disability 31 Mar 1987; Ostapenko missing, declared dead 12 Aug 1986; Babych ARS I survived; Yakovenko opened valve 12, working.

question: Describe the efforts to deal with water and heat under the reactor in May-July 1986.
answer: Fear of steam explosion; bubbler pool drained 25-26 May (valve 12, ~3,050 m3 pumped by PS-115F); nitrogen injection from 24 May (70 t); foundation temperature peaked ~271 C 28 May then fell; tunnel 136 m by miners (4 Jun-2 Jul) and heat-exchanger slab installed 2 Jul, never activated.

question: Summarize the use of robots on the roofs.
answer: MRK-2 (NIIKRE) from 22 Aug, low productivity; Varnland R-40 arrived 29 Aug, failed 6 Sep (electronics, >1,000 R/h); MRK-2 unit 01 fell 19 Sep; soldiers cleared zones L and M 20 Sep-1 Oct; replacement MRK-2 (factory 0007) registered as ROB-MRK2-01 on 3 Oct.

question: What changes were made to the RBMK-type units after the accident?
answer: Min ORM 30 rods, continuous ORM display, ban below 700 MW, 80 additional absorbers, 2.4% fuel, modified rods (no water column), EPS 12 s, no blocking of trips; restart limit 3,000 MWt.

question: Trace the history of the warning about the control-rod effect.
answer: Observed Dnestrovsk 1983 (report not in corpus); NIIKRE memo 14 Oct 1985 (Yarosh) to OKB-Kanal and 3 stations incl. V-NPS; Levchenko reply 12 Nov 1985: 0.2-0.3 beta, no instructions; commission 1986 mentions design features only secondarily; memo raised at trial (17 Jul 1987), judge ruled design irrelevant; press Sep 1987; GNI revised analysis Nov 1987 makes it a decisive cause; OKB-Kanal disputes.

question: Who were the defendants and what were their positions on 17 May 1986?
answer: Hrytsenko (director), Savchenko (chief engineer), Zuev (deputy chief engineer Units 3-4, led test), G. A. Morozov (station shift supervisor), Sidorenko (head reactor shop No. 2), Fedorov (resident GNI inspector, on leave 5-25 May).

question: What were the Shelter's design, construction and condition by mid-1987?
answer: Variant 'cascade wall + girder' (30 Jun 1986); SU-219 formed 10 Jun; girder B1 installed 28 Oct; closed 9 Dec, accepted 14 Dec 1986; ~394,000 m3 concrete, ~9,500 t steel; sealing done 26 Feb 1987 except axes 46-50; Jul 1987: west wall unknown, openings 100-1,000 m2, fuel location uncertain, 24/32 sensors, life 20-30 y.

question: Who was in charge of Vereskovo NPS (performing the director's duties) on 15 July 1986?
answer: S. L. Bondar, deputy director, temporarily performing the duties of director (2-28 Jul 1986).

question: Who was chief engineer of the station in August 1986?
answer: P. A. Orlov as acting chief engineer (from 9 Jun; confirmed 6 Oct 1986).

question: Who chaired the Government Commission on 10 June 1986?
answer: V. A. Demidov (from 3 Jun 1986).

question: Who was the station director in June 1986?
answer: V. S. Hrytsenko (still director until 2 Jul 1986, although the Government Commission directed the work).

question: What was the dose limit for a seconded worker at the station on 20 January 1987?
answer: Ministry limit was 10 rem/year from 1 Jan 1987, but the station order kept the 25-rem limit for persons whose 1986 cards were not closed until 1 Feb 1987 - answer depends on whether the card was closed.

question: What was the head of the cadres department's surname in December 1986?
answer: Kuzmina (V. S. Kuzmina); became Osipova on 14 Feb 1987.

question: Which units of the station were operating in January 1987?
answer: Units 1 and 2 (restarted 1 Oct and 5 Nov 1986); Unit 3 shut down until 4 Dec 1987; Unit 4 = Shelter.

question: What was the zone status of Ruda Vereskivska in September 1986 and in December 1987?
answer: Sep 1986: strict control zone (from 1 Aug 1986), not evacuated. Dec 1987: still strict control zone with voluntary resettlement since 1 Sep 1987.

question: What position did L. T. Golub hold in May 1987?
answer: Lt. Colonel, deputy head of the regional fire directorate (from 1 Apr 1987).

question: Who was Unit 4 shift supervisor on the evening shift of 16 May 1986?
answer: I. Romanov (Shift 4), with SIUR M. Kalnysh.

question: What is the current (Dec 1987) official position on the cause, and what did the 1986 report say?
answer: 1986 commission and court: operator violations (six listed) main cause. Nov 1987 GNI working group: design deficiencies (positive void coefficient ~+4.5 beta, rod tip effect, no continuous ORM display) decisive in combination with personnel actions; several 'violations' were not prohibited. OKB-Kanal disputes (Dec 1987) - so contested; the most recent regulator analysis is the GNI report.

question: What is the current ORM requirement for Units 1-3 and how did it change?
answer: Not less than 30 rods, shutdown below 30, shown continuously (1986 revision); previously 15 rods (1983 regulations), with ORM given every 5-10 min.

question: What is the current status of the Units 5-6 project?
answer: Terminated 31 Oct 1987 (suspended 18 Jun 1986); directorate dissolved; ~0.62 billion rubles written off; staff to Lisogorsk.

question: What is ROB-MRK2-01 today?
answer: The replacement MRK-2 robot (factory No. 0007), registered under the ID of the robot that fell from the roof on 19 Sep 1986.

question: Where do station staff live now, and what was promised in May 1986?
answer: Rotation camp Berezovy Gai (15 days on/off); new town Lisogorsk under construction from Oct 1987. In May 1986 residents were told the evacuation was temporary (3 days).

question: What is the current registry number format for liquidators and how does it relate to 1986 cards?
answer: VR87-RR-NNNNN since 1 Mar 1987; 1986 L86-###### numbers kept as 'previous number'; 118,600 cards -> 104,300 records.

question: What is the current number of monitoring sensors working in the Shelter, compared with earlier reports?
At what time did the explosion occur, and why do sources differ?
answer: About 01:31:45 and 01:31:48 (two explosions). Log '01:32' is rounded; trial testimony approximate; Vega and seismic agree.

question: What was the ORM just before the test?
answer: About 7 rods (7.2 at 01:22:30), not 15-20 as Zuev stated.

question: How many people died as a result of the accident by end-1986?
answer: 32 by internal records (official 31, omitting a Kyiv hospital death).

question: On what date was Hrytsenko dismissed?
answer: 2 July 1986 (order No. 314-k); 30 June on the cadres card and 'end of June' in the press are wrong.

question: When did Belov become director?

question: How many buses evacuated Vereskovsk?
answer: 1,216 (dispatch record / Karpenko); 1,100 was the plan.

question: When did Unit 3 restart, given the press says November 1987?
answer: 4 Dec 1987, 06:40 (telegram, log).

question: Was the Shelter completed 'ahead of schedule' as the press said?
answer: No: original target Oct 1986; closed 9 Dec, accepted 14 Dec 1986, sealing to Feb 1987.

question: What dose did Lt. Rudenko receive?
answer: 8.6 Gy (biodosimetry, Clinic No. 4); 15 Gy in the award submission and >4 Gy initial estimate are not authoritative.

question: Who decided to continue the test after the power drop?
answer: Not determinable: log has no name; Zuev blames Tkachuk (deceased); Melnyk says Zuev insisted; Babych says nobody explicitly decided.

question: Was AZ-5 pressed as a routine end of test or in reaction to a power rise?
answer: Not established (GNI 1987 states this); testimony conflicts.

question: How high did the power go?
answer: Unknown: commission ~100x nominal, Varnland at least ~10x, GNI 1987 says cannot be determined.

question: How many tests of the turbine rundown were done before 1986?
answer: Three (1982, 1984, 1985) per commission; Zuev said two.

question: When was Unit 4 commissioned?
answer: Grid connection 22 Dec 1983 (first criticality Dec 1983); commercial operation 30 Mar 1984.

question: What figure did the director's telegram give for dose rate on site?
answer: 1,100 uR/s in the original (03:45); 1,000 in the 04:20 retransmission and in the commission minutes.

question: When was the fire put out?
answer: Roof fires: localized 02:20, extinguished 05:00, last hot spots 06:35 on 17 May. Graphite fire in the reactor: about 29 May.

question: How many patients went to Kyiv?
Does the 15-rod ORM limit apply only at nominal power?
answer: No - 'under all operating conditions' per the regulations.

question: What is the population of Vereskovsk and why do figures differ?
answer: 47,800 permanent (1 Jan 1986) + ~2,100 temporary; 44,600 evacuated by bus; 45,000 planning figure; ~49,000 Vienna.

question: Is 'Gritzenko' in the foreign press the same person as V. S. Hrytsenko and 'Gritsenko'?
answer: Yes - Ukrainian/Russian/foreign spellings of the director Viktor Semyonovich Hrytsenko (VNPS-00012).

question: Who is the 'V. Morozov' who signed reconnaissance report No. 3 of 18 May?
answer: Major Vasily I. Morozov, commander of the radiation reconnaissance battalion - not Vladimir N. Morozov, head of the station dosimetry service (who signed the 17 May report).

question: Who is G. A. Morozov, and is he related to the dosimetry Morozov?
answer: Grigory A. Morozov, station shift supervisor, convicted (5 years). Different person from V. N. Morozov (dosimetry) and Major V. I. Morozov; no relation documented.

question: What is 'the third pump on the left side' / 'the noisy one'?
answer: U4-MCP-03.

question: Are 'Vega-M' and 'VPC-4/II' the same system?
answer: Yes - the Unit 4 plant computer (station name vs design-institute designation).

question: Is V. S. Kuzmina the same person as V. S. Osipova?
answer: Yes - head of cadres department, surname changed on marriage 14 Feb 1987 (VNPS-00088).

question: Are Melnik and Melnyk the same person?

question: Who is 'M. K.', author of the notes for new SIURs, and who is 'Petro'?

question: What is 'the thousand meter'?

question: How many confirmed ARS cases by degree, and how many died?

question: How many people were evacuated from villages within 10 km (incl. Verbivka and Ostriv)?
How many ARS deaths occurred in Clinic No. 4 by 20 June 1986?
Total length of the tunnel under Unit 4?
Why was the test run at much lower power than planned?
answer: Dispatcher held the unit at 1,600 MW for ~9 h, causing xenon buildup; the reduction resumed at 23:10; at 00:28 during regulator transfer power fell to ~30 MW; with xenon the operators could only raise it to ~200 MW by withdrawing rods, which also drove the ORM down.

question: Why was the radiation danger underestimated in the first hours?
answer: RKS-4 meters saturated at 4 R/h; the high-range VR-1000 was locked in the Unit 1 safe until 03:50; the director reported 1,100 uR/s (~4 R/h, the scale top) as 'normal'; Zuev believed the reactor intact.

question: What was first suspected as the initiating event, and why was it rejected?
answer: MCP cavitation (8 pumps, high flow, MCP-3 vibration history) - examined by the working group 20 May; rejected by recorded flows (commission Jul 1986, GNI 1987). Hydrogen explosion also suspected early.

question: Why was the rundown test needed at all?
answer: Diesel generators took 58-65 s to accept load; rotor rundown energy was meant to bridge 45-60 s for MCPs and feedwater pumps.

question: How did the Varnland detection lead to the announcement?
answer: Skarvik portal alarms 07:10 local (05:10 UTC) 19 May; own leak suspected then ruled out by 10:00; fuel nuclides; trajectory to the east; embassy inquiries from 14:00 Moscow time got 'no information'; official statement at 21:00.

question: Why was Unit 3 restart delayed repeatedly?
answer: Central hall dose rates above norm; separate ventilation untested; GNI required Shelter monitoring completed; recontamination from Shelter roof in July 1987; ventilation accepted with remarks Sep 1987.

question: Why is lead now considered a bad choice?
answer: Only part reached the shaft; high temperatures evaporated lead, adding toxic contamination on site and in Lisove district; release drop attributed mainly to fire exhaustion.

question: Why did Lisove have to be evacuated three weeks after the accident?
answer: Soil sampling found Cs-137 up to 20-25 Ci/km2 in the NW part; decision No. 14 (6 Jun) -> evacuation 7 Jun.

question: Why was the Unit 3 roof cleared by soldiers instead of robots?
answer: R-40 electronics failed 6 Sep in >1,000 R/h; MRK-2 fell from roof 19 Sep; decision No. 41 same day ordered manual clearing.

question: Convert the 1986 dose limit of 25 rem to sieverts.
